_readme: This contract defines the ephemeral agent_session_info wire vocabulary. The Worker broadcasts this map with seq -1 and never persists it. total_cost_usd and context_usage use wireSessionInfoToUpdates. rate_limits carries one atomic update with an explicit mode and values map. wireRateLimitUpdateFromSessionInfo decodes it. Generation progress, running_tool, and goal_progress also use focused decoders. These values belong to the progress, chat, and goal stores. Go writes every token here, and TypeScript reads it. A token mismatch silently stops an update, so the generated copies must not drift. Object-valued keys also specify their nested fields. One-side-only Go tokens stay outside this contract until the browser reads them. Issues 433 and 434 track the excluded pi_* and zcode_api_retry tokens. running_tool omits tool_name and subagent_type because the tool card reads both from its persisted row. It carries output_tail, which contains the latest tool output bytes. output_truncated states that the Worker dropped earlier bytes. This state is ephemeral, like elapsed_seconds. The finished row retains the complete provider frame. agent_session_id and span_id together identify a running tool row. A span ID is unique only inside one provider session. The browser keys live progress by this pair, which prevents cross-session attachment. TotalCostUsd must keep the total_cost_usd token. Claude Code writes that token in persisted result lines, and a Go struct tag also uses the literal. checkSessionInfo pins the token. Pi owns its tokens alias for context_tokens, so pi-protocol.json is its possible contract. goal_progress is the volatile half of a session goal. Codex updates it after each completed tool call. The durable objective, status, and identity stay on the agent row and broadcast only on a transition. Every field is optional because providers report different sets. An absent field must stay absent instead of becoming zero.
